blocks.heading: The city that clothed the world
blocks.html:
For three centuries Leicester’s framework knitters and factories made stockings, socks, underwear and knitwear for Britain and beyond. Corah’s St Margaret’s Works and the Wolsey brand made the city a byword for knitted goods.

That heritage lives on in the city’s knitters, garment makers, dyers and machine engineers.

sections.h2: Sewing machines, wool and workshop supplies for the UK
sections.html:
UK SEW is a free guide to the British sewing and knitting world. Whether you are buying your first machine after watching The Great British Sewing Bee, sourcing a bobbin case for a 40-year-old Singer, or keeping a row of industrial lockstitch machines running, we bring the options together in one place.

  • Sewing machines: mechanical, computerised and heavy-duty machines for home use.
  • Industrial sewing machines: lockstitch, overlock, coverstitch and specialist machines for trade.
  • Parts and needles: needle systems, bobbins, feet, belts and motors.
  • Wool and yarn: UK yarn weights, fibres and how to choose.
  • Repairs and servicing and machine hire.

Good advice comes from people who mend machines for a living. Our guides lean on Leicester’s workshop tradition, including PK Sewing Machines on St Saviours Road, a family business since 1982 that sells, services and repairs domestic and industrial machines and keeps a large parts department.

sections.h2: Leicester: the city that clothed the world
sections.html: Framework knitting reached Leicestershire in the 1600s, and by the 1800s Leicester was famous for stockings, underwear and knitwear. Firms such as N. Corah & Sons, whose St Margaret’s Works was one of the largest hosiery factories in Britain, and Wolsey, named after Cardinal Wolsey who is buried at Leicester Abbey, made the city a byword for knitted goods. Explore Leicester’s hosiery heritage and our UK hosiery sector reading list.

sections.h2: Hosiery, knitwear and the machines behind them
sections.html: Hosiery means knitted legwear and underwear: socks, tights and stockings. Today’s socks are knitted on circular machines and finished on linking and toe-closing machines, while garments are sewn on overlockers and coverstitch machines, the same types that keep Leicester’s workrooms busy. Read our hosiery and knitwear guide, what denier means and how socks are made.

faqs.q: Where can I get a sewing machine serviced in Leicester?
faqs.a: Our featured specialist, PK Sewing Machines at 415 St Saviours Road, Leicester LE5 4HH, services and repairs domestic and industrial machines. Its website lists servicing from £35. Call 0116 273 6552 to book.

faqs.q: Do your reviews include customer star ratings?
faqs.a: No. Our reviews are editorial overviews of brands and machine types. We do not publish invented ratings or customer reviews.
